definition_en: a long narrow passage inside a building, or a narrow strip of land between two areas
core_image: 一条长长的通道，两侧的门一扇接一扇，尽头透进白光
scene: 医院三楼的走廊很长，尽头那扇窗透进一片白光。A nurse walked quickly down the corridor.
sceneCN: 这里 corridor 指「走廊」（第 1 个义项：建筑物内连接房间的长通道）；句意是一位护士快步走过走廊。

collocations.phrase: at the end of the corridor

derivatives.zh: 信使；快递员（与 corridor 同源于「跑」）
光标（同源词，本指奔跑者）

senses.title: A passage inside a building
senses.definition: a long narrow passage that connects rooms in a building
senses.definitionCN: 建筑物内连接各个房间的狭长通道
senses.example: A nurse walked quickly down the corridor.
senses.exampleCN: 一位护士快步走过走廊。
senses.why: A building needs a spine so that its rooms can be one body.
senses.whyCN: 建筑需要一根脊梁，房间才能连成一个身体。

senses.title: A strip of land
senses.definition: a narrow piece of land that joins two larger areas
senses.definitionCN: 连接两片较大区域的狭长土地
senses.example: The road runs through a narrow corridor of land.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路穿过一条狭长地带。
senses.why: Countries also need passages, and they guard them like doors.
senses.whyCN: 国家也需要通道，并像守门一样守着它们。

senses.title: The aisle of a train
senses.definition: the narrow walking space between seats in a train or plane
senses.definitionCN: 火车或飞机座位之间供人行走的窄道
senses.example: He stood in the corridor with his ticket.
senses.exampleCN: 他拿着车票站在车厢过道里。
senses.why: Even a moving box needs a line along which people pass.
senses.whyCN: 即使是一只移动的盒子，也需要一条让人通过的线。

intro.en: Corridor comes from Italian corridore, a runner or running place, from correre, to run, and Latin currere.
intro.cn: corridor 来自意大利语 corridore（奔跑者、跑道），源自 correre（跑）与拉丁语 currere。

items.en: Currere meant to run.
items.cn: currere 意为奔跑。

items.en: Corridore named a runner or a place for running.
items.cn: corridore 指奔跑的人或供奔跑的地方。

items.en: French corridor named a narrow passage in a fortress.
items.cn: 法语 corridor 指堡垒中的狭窄通道。

items.en: English corridor first meant a covered walk or gallery.
items.cn: 英语 corridor 最初指有顶的步道或长廊。

items.en: It now means any long passage, in a building or on a map.
items.cn: 今天它指任何长通道，无论在大楼里还是地图上。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the running base curr-, and the meaning group names other ways through a building.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示奔跑的词基 curr-，近义组列出其他穿过建筑的说法。

entries.definition: to eat away metal slowly
to drive animals into an enclosure
a ring of light around the sun
a passage just inside the front door
a narrow way from one place to another
entries.definitionCN: 从一处通向另一处的窄道

entries.definition: the space between rows of seats

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a long passage lined with doors, then move to a narrow strip of land and to a train aisle.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两侧都是门的长通道开始，再到狭长地带，最后到车厢过道。

normal.en: Corridor comes from a word for running, so it is a place made for moving.
normal.cn: corridor 源自表示奔跑的词，所以它是为移动而设的地方。

normal.en: A corridor has two rows of doors and no chairs.
normal.cn: 走廊有两排门，却没有椅子。

normal.en: Hospitals keep corridors long so that beds can pass.
normal.cn: 医院把走廊修得长，是为了让病床通过。

normal.en: A land corridor is a hallway between two countries.
normal.cn: 陆上走廊就是两国之间的一条过道。

normal.en: The double r in the middle keeps the word running.
normal.cn: 中间的两个 r 让这个词一直向前跑。

abstract.en: Picture a line of doors standing one behind another.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇扇门一层层排在身后。

abstract.en: Picture a thin neck of land joining two wide rooms.
abstract.cn: 想象一条细长的陆地，把两片宽阔的土地连起来。

abstract.en: Picture light at the far end of a very long tunnel.
abstract.cn: 想象一条很长隧道的尽头有光。

examples.en: A nurse walked quickly down the corridor.
examples.cn: 一位护士快步走过走廊。

examples.en: Their office is at the end of the corridor.
examples.cn: 他们的办公室在走廊尽头。

examples.en: The train corridor was full of luggage.
examples.cn: 火车过道里堆满了行李。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 corridor 记成「能跑的道」：两侧是门、中间能一路跑到尽头，就是走廊。

root: 源自意大利语 corridore（奔跑者、跑道），来自 correre（跑），再上溯到拉丁语 currere（奔跑），本指供人穿行的长道。

sensesIntro.en: From a passage between rooms, to a thin strip of land, and at last to the aisle of a moving carriage.
sensesIntro.cn: 从房间之间的通道，到一条细长的土地，最后到移动车厢里的过道。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long narrow passage with doors on both sides.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条长而窄的通道，两侧都是门。

branches.en: The corridor turns separate rooms into one building.
branches.cn: 走廊把一个个房间变成一栋完整的建筑。

branches.en: A narrow strip of land turns two areas into neighbours.
branches.cn: 一条狭长土地把两片区域变成邻居。

branches.en: An aisle lets people pass while the carriage moves.
branches.cn: 过道让人们在车厢移动时仍能通行。

branches.en: Both are thin lines that join larger spaces.
branches.cn: 两者都是连接较大空间的细线。

branches.en: Land corridor and train aisle are both narrow routes of passage.
branches.cn: 陆上走廊与车厢过道都是狭窄的通行路线。

intro.en: Corridor is built on Latin currere, to run, through Italian corridore, a running place.
intro.cn: corridor 建立在拉丁语 currere（奔跑）之上，经意大利语 corridore（跑道）而来。

latinIntro.en: The running base curr- also appears in current, cursor and excursion.
latinIntro.cn: 表示奔跑的词基 curr- 也出现在 current、cursor 与 excursion 中。

items.meaning: a train with a side passage
items.example: The corridor train stops at every town.
items.exampleCN: 这趟走廊式列车逢站就停。

items.meaning: a carriage with a side passage
items.example: We sat in the corridor coach.
items.exampleCN: 我们坐在走廊式车厢里。

items.meaning: a path or direction of movement
water or air that runs forward
a moving mark on a screen

definition_en: the money needed to buy or make something, the loss suffered for a gain, or to have a price
core_image: 一张价签挂在货物上，背后还压着一本看不见的账
scene: 装修报价单摊在桌上，木地板那一项比预期高出一截。The repairs will cost more than we planned.
sceneCN: 这里 cost 指「花费」（第 3 个义项：需要付出某笔钱）；句意是这次维修的花费会超出我们的计划。

senses.title: The money needed
senses.definition: the amount of money that must be paid to buy or make something
senses.definitionCN: 为购买或制造某物必须支付的金额
senses.example: The cost of the ticket surprised us.
senses.exampleCN: 票价让我们吃了一惊。
senses.why: Every object carries an invisible price tag on its back.
senses.whyCN: 每件物品背后都挂着一张看不见的价签。

senses.title: What a gain takes from you
senses.definition: the loss or damage suffered in order to gain something
senses.definitionCN: 为获得某物而承受的损失或损害
senses.example: He won the match at the cost of his health.
senses.exampleCN: 他赢了比赛，代价是健康。
senses.why: Every victory is paid for with something that is not money.
senses.whyCN: 每一场胜利都要用钱以外的东西来支付。

senses.title: To have a price
senses.definition: to have a particular price, or to make someone lose something
senses.definitionCN: 价格为某数，或使某人失去某物
senses.example: The repairs will cost more than we planned.
senses.exampleCN: 这次维修的花费会超出我们的计划。
senses.why: The price reaches out from the object and takes money from your hand.
senses.whyCN: 价格从物品那边伸出手，把你手中的钱拿走。

intro.en: Cost comes from Latin constare, to stand firm or stand at a price, through Old French coster, to cost.
intro.cn: cost 来自拉丁语 constare（立定、值某个价钱），经古法语 coster（值…钱）进入英语。

items.en: Constare meant to stand together or stand firm.
items.cn: constare 意为共同站立或稳稳立住。

items.en: The same verb came to mean to stand at a certain price.
items.cn: 同一个动词后来表示标价为某个数目。

items.en: Coster meant to cost or be bought for a sum.
items.cn: coster 意为值多少钱、以某价购得。

items.en: English cost named the price paid for a thing.
items.cn: 英语 cost 指为某物付出的价钱。

items.en: It also names the price paid in effort, time or health.
items.cn: 它也指用精力、时间或健康付出的代价。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words in -ost or -ast, and the meaning group names other words for what is paid.
note.cn: 形近组收集以 -ost 或 -ast 结尾的短词，近义组列出其他表示所付之物的说法。

entries.definition: the land beside the sea
to throw something with force
a piece of outer clothing
the money asked for a thing
money spent on a purpose
the money demanded for a service

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a price tag, then move to a victory paid for in health and to a repair that empties a wallet.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一张价签开始，再到用健康换来的胜利，最后到掏空钱包的维修。

normal.en: Cost is the price tag plus everything the price tag hides.
normal.cn: cost 是价签，也是价签藏起来的一切。

normal.en: The past tense does not change: it cost, it has cost.
normal.cn: 过去式不变：it cost，it has cost。

normal.en: Cheap things often cost more in the end.
normal.cn: 便宜的东西，最后往往花费更多。

normal.en: A costly mistake is one whose price arrives later.
normal.cn: 代价惨重的错误，就是账单迟到的错误。

normal.en: Effort, time and sleep can all be costs.
normal.cn: 精力、时间和睡眠都可以是代价。

abstract.en: Picture a coin lying on one pan of a balance.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币躺在天平的一端。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt longer than the thing you bought.
abstract.cn: 想象一张比你买的东西还长的收据。

abstract.en: Picture a door marked free with a small lock on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇写着免费的门，上面挂着一把小锁。

examples.en: The repairs will cost more than we planned.
examples.cn: 这次维修的花费会超出我们的计划。

examples.en: The ticket costs a week of his wages.
examples.cn: 这张票要花掉他一周的工资。

examples.en: He won the match at the cost of his health.
examples.cn: 他赢了比赛，代价是健康。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cost 记成「扣死他」：价格一扣，钱就没了，所以是花费与代价。

root: 源自拉丁语 constare（共同立定、值某个价钱），经古法语 coster 进入英语，本指物品所值之价，后引申为一切代价。

sensesIntro.en: From money on a tag, to a loss that is not money, and at last to the act of taking money from a pocket.
sensesIntro.cn: 从价签上的钱，到不是钱的损失，最后到从口袋里拿走钱这一动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a price tag with a hidden ledger behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张价签，背后压着一本看不见的账。

branches.en: A sum of money is named before the deal.
branches.cn: 交易之前先说出一个钱数。

branches.en: Something other than money is taken away.
branches.cn: 被拿走的不是钱，而是别的东西。

branches.en: The verb makes the object reach into your pocket.
branches.cn: 动词使物品伸手进你的口袋。

branches.en: The noun and the verb name the same money from two sides.
branches.cn: 名词与动词从两侧说同一笔钱。

branches.en: To cost can mean to take away health, time or peace.
branches.cn: 花费也可以指拿走健康、时间或安宁。

intro.en: Cost is a short base word from Latin constare, to stand at a price, with many modern compounds.
intro.cn: cost 是来自拉丁语 constare（标价）的短词根词，现代又生出许多复合词。

latinIntro.en: The standing base sta- also appears in constant, stable and stand.
latinIntro.cn: 表示站立的词基 sta- 也出现在 constant、stable 与 stand 中。

items.meaning: giving good value for the money
the price paid by the seller

items.exampleCN: 削减开支救了这家公司。

definition_en: a small house, especially in the countryside, or a small house used for holidays
core_image: 一栋石头小屋，茅草屋顶上飘着一缕细烟
scene: 雨落在茅草顶上，烟囱冒出细细一缕烟。They spent the summer in a small cottage by the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 cottage 指「乡村小屋」（第 1 个义项：乡下的小房子）；句意是他们在海边的一间小屋度过了夏天。

senses.title: A small country house
senses.definition: a small simple house, especially in the countryside
senses.definitionCN: 尤指乡下的简朴小房子
senses.example: They spent the summer in a small cottage by the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在海边的一间小屋度过了夏天。
senses.why: Small walls and a low roof keep a country life warm.
senses.whyCN: 矮墙低顶，把乡间的生活捂得暖暖的。

senses.title: A house for holidays
senses.definition: a small house that people rent or keep for short holidays
senses.definitionCN: 人们租用或留着短期度假的小房子
senses.example: We rented a cottage in the hills for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在山里租了一间小屋住了一周。
senses.why: A holiday needs a roof smaller than the life you left behind.
senses.whyCN: 度假需要一个比原先生活更小的屋顶。

intro.en: Cottage goes back to Old English cot, a small hut, with the French ending -age added in medieval times.
intro.cn: cottage 可追溯到古英语 cot（小屋），中世纪时加上法语词尾 -age。

items.en: Cot meant a small hut or shelter.
items.cn: cot 意为小茅屋或遮蔽处。

items.en: Cotagium named a small dwelling with a little land.
items.cn: cotagium 指带一小块土地的小住所。

items.en: Cottage named the house of a country worker.
items.cn: cottage 指乡间劳动者的住房。

items.en: English cottage meant a small rural house.
items.cn: 英语 cottage 指乡间的小房子。

items.en: It now also names small houses kept for holidays.
items.cn: 今天它也指留着度假用的小屋。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words near the shape of cottage, and the meaning group names other small dwellings.
note.cn: 形近组收集形状接近 cottage 的短词，近义组列出其他小型住所。

entries.definition: a place of higher or further education
entries.definitionCN: 高等教育或继续教育的场所

entries.definition: a poor farm worker with a small cottage
entries.definitionCN: 只有一间小屋的贫苦农业雇工

entries.definition: a small shelter for birds or animals
a small simple wooden house
a very small and simple shelter
a small house used for hunting or holidays

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a stone wall and a low roof, then move to a rented holiday house in the hills.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从石头墙和低屋顶开始，再到山里租来的度假小屋。

normal.en: Cot is an old word for a small hut, and -age makes it a place.
normal.cn: cot 是表示小茅屋的古词，加 -age 就成了一个地方。

normal.en: A cottage is smaller than a house and warmer than a tent.
normal.cn: 小屋比房子小，却比帐篷暖和。

normal.en: Think of a low door, a small window and smoke from the chimney.
normal.cn: 想想一扇矮门、一扇小窗和烟囱里的烟。

normal.en: A cottage garden grows flowers beside the vegetables.
normal.cn: 乡舍花园在蔬菜旁边种着花。

normal.en: Cottage and college look alike but live very different lives.
normal.cn: cottage 与 college 长得像，过的却是很不一样的日子。

abstract.en: Picture rain sliding down a roof of yellow straw.
abstract.cn: 想象雨水顺着金黄茅草屋顶滑下。

abstract.en: Picture one warm window in a dark green valley.
abstract.cn: 想象墨绿山谷里的一扇暖窗。

abstract.en: Picture a key too small to open anything but a cottage door.
abstract.cn: 想象一把小得只能开小屋门的钥匙。

examples.en: They spent the summer in a small cottage by the sea.
examples.cn: 他们在海边的一间小屋度过了夏天。

examples.en: We rented a cottage in the hills for a week.
examples.cn: 我们在山里租了一间小屋住了一周。

examples.en: A narrow path leads to the old cottage.
examples.cn: 一条窄路通向那间老屋。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cottage 记成 cot（小床、小屋）加 tage：一张小床就能安顿下来的地方，就是村舍小屋。

root: 源自古英语 cot（小茅屋、棚舍），中世纪加法语词尾 -age，本指乡间劳动者的小住所，后泛指村舍与度假小屋。

sensesIntro.en: From a worker's small house in the country, to a small house rented for a few weeks.
sensesIntro.cn: 从乡间劳动者的小住所，到租来住几周的小屋。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone cottage with a low thatched roof and thin smoke.
core.cn: 核心意象：石头小屋，低矮的茅草顶上升起一缕细烟。

branches.en: A country family lives close to the ground and the weather.
branches.cn: 乡间人家贴着土地与天气生活。

branches.en: A visitor borrows that small life for a short time.
branches.cn: 来客短暂地借用那种小日子。

branches.en: Both are small roofs, one lived in and one borrowed.
branches.cn: 两者都是小屋顶，一个常住，一个借用。

branches.en: The garden and the chimney are part of its picture.
branches.cn: 花园与烟囱都是它画面的一部分。

branches.en: Holiday cottages keep old shapes for new guests.
branches.cn: 度假小屋用旧形状迎接新客人。

intro.en: Cottage joins the old base cot, a hut, with the French noun ending -age, meaning a place.
intro.cn: cottage 由古词基 cot（小屋）加法语名词词尾 -age（场所）构成。

latinIntro.en: The dwelling base cot- also appears in cot, cote and cottage.
latinIntro.cn: 表示住所的词基 cot- 也出现在 cot、cote 与 cottage 中。

items.meaning: a person who lives in a cottage
items.example: The cottager waved from the gate.
items.exampleCN: 住小屋的人在门口挥手。

items.meaning: work done at home in small units
items.meaningCN: 在家中分散进行的小规模生产
items.example: Weaving began as a cottage industry.
items.exampleCN: 织布最初是家庭手工业。

items.meaning: soft white cheese made at home
items.example: He ate cottage cheese for lunch.
The cottage garden smell of roses.
items.exampleCN: 乡舍花园里有玫瑰的香气。

items.meaning: a dish of meat under mashed potato
items.meaningCN: 上面铺土豆泥的肉馅饼
items.exampleCN: 她烤了一个肉馅土豆饼。

items.meaning: a small simple bed or hut
items.example: A cot stood by the wall.

definition_en: the soft white fibre of a plant, the cloth made from it, or thread spun from it
core_image: 枝头绽开一团白云似的棉絮，手指一捏就散成细丝
scene: 老妇人把一团白软的纤维捻成线，一圈圈绕在木轴上。She wore a plain cotton shirt to the market.
sceneCN: 这里 cotton 指「棉布」（第 2 个义项：用棉花织成的布）；句意是她穿着朴素的棉布衬衫去市场。

senses.title: The plant fibre
senses.definition: the soft white fibre that grows around the seeds of a tall plant
senses.definitionCN: 长在高大植物种子周围的柔软白色纤维
senses.example: The fields were white with cotton.
senses.exampleCN: 田野被棉花染成一片白。
senses.why: A plant wraps its seeds in white and humans borrow that coat.
senses.whyCN: 植物给种子裹上白色外衣，人类借用了这层衣服。

senses.title: The woven cloth
senses.definition: cloth made from cotton fibre
senses.definitionCN: 用棉花纤维织成的布
senses.example: She wore a plain cotton shirt to the market.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿着朴素的棉布衬衫去市场。
senses.why: Soft fibre becomes strong cloth when threads cross.
senses.whyCN: 柔软的纤维在经纬交错时变成结实的布。

senses.title: The spun thread
senses.definition: thread made by twisting cotton fibres together
senses.definitionCN: 把棉花纤维捻在一起做成的线
senses.example: The needle needs a length of cotton.
senses.exampleCN: 针上需要一段棉线。
senses.why: Twist a cloud of fibre and it becomes a line you can sew with.
senses.whyCN: 把一团纤维一捻，就成了能缝东西的线。

intro.en: Cotton comes from Arabic qutn, which passed through Italian cotone and Old French coton into English.
intro.cn: cotton 来自阿拉伯语 qutn，经意大利语 cotone 与古法语 coton 进入英语。

items.en: Qutn named the cotton plant and its fibre.
items.cn: qutn 指棉花这种植物及其纤维。

items.en: Cotone carried the word into Mediterranean trade.

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a white ball on a branch, then move to a shirt and to a needle's thread.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从枝头一团白絮开始，再到一件衬衫，最后到针上的棉线。

normal.en: Cotton looks like a small cloud that grew on a stem.
normal.cn: cotton 像一朵长在茎上的小云。

normal.en: The same word is the plant, the fibre, the thread and the shirt.
normal.cn: 同一个词既是植株，也是纤维、棉线和衬衫。

normal.en: Cotton is uncountable, so you say a cotton shirt, not a cotton.
normal.cn: cotton 不可数，所以要说 a cotton shirt，而不是 a cotton。

normal.en: Pick cotton by hand and your fingers learn the word.
normal.cn: 用手采一次棉花，手指就记住了这个词。

normal.en: Two t letters sit in the middle like two bolls on one stem.

abstract.en: Picture a thread pulled from a cloud.

abstract.en: Picture a shirt breathing in a warm wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一件衬衫在暖风里轻轻呼吸。

examples.en: The fields were white with cotton.

sensesIntro.en: From fibre around a seed, to cloth on a back, and at last to the thin line that holds a button.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white boll of cotton opening on a dry stem.
core.cn: 核心意象：干枯茎上绽开的一团白棉。

branches.en: The plant gives a soft white coat around its seeds.
branches.cn: 植物在种子周围长出一层柔软的白衣。

branches.en: Crossed threads turn that coat into cloth.
branches.cn: 交错的线把那层衣服变成布。

branches.en: A twisted few fibres become a line for sewing.
branches.cn: 几根纤维一捻，就成了缝东西的线。

branches.en: Fibre and cloth are the same material at two stages.
branches.cn: 纤维与布是同一材料的前后两个阶段。

branches.en: Cloth and thread both begin as a white ball in a field.
branches.cn: 布与线都始于田里的一团白。

intro.en: Cotton is a borrowed base word from Arabic, extended by English compounds and suffixes.

latinIntro.en: Though not Latin, the word travelled with cloth trade through Italy and France.

definition_en: the past form of can, used for past ability, for possibility, or for a polite request
core_image: 一个孩子仰头看树，脚尖一蹬就够到了最高的枝
scene: 孩子盯着树上的风筝，跳了两次还是够不着。When I was young, I could climb that tree in seconds.
sceneCN: 这里 could 指「能够」（第 1 个义项：过去有能力做某事）；句意是我小时候几秒钟就能爬上那棵树。

derivatives.zh: 将会；愿意（相关情态动词）

senses.title: Past ability
senses.definition: used as the past form of can to say that someone was able to do something
senses.definitionCN: 作为 can 的过去式，表示某人过去有能力做某事
senses.example: When I was young, I could climb that tree in seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 我小时候几秒钟就能爬上那棵树。
senses.why: Memory keeps a door open to strength we no longer have.
senses.whyCN: 记忆为那份已不再有的力气留着一扇门。

senses.title: What is possible
senses.definition: used to say that something is possible, though not certain
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示某事有可能，但不确定
senses.example: The keys could be in your coat.
senses.exampleCN: 钥匙可能在你大衣里。
senses.why: A door left a little open lets many futures through.
senses.whyCN: 一扇虚掩的门，能让许多种未来通过。

senses.title: A polite request
senses.definition: used to ask for something or to make a suggestion politely
senses.definitionCN: 用于礼貌地提出请求或建议
senses.example: Could you close the window, please?
senses.exampleCN: 请你把窗关上好吗？
senses.why: Softening the voice is how English opens a door without pushing.
senses.whyCN: 把语气放软，是英语不推门也能让门打开的方式。

intro.en: Could began as the past tense of can; its l was later added by writers who copied would and should.
intro.cn: could 原本是 can 的过去式，后来人们仿照 would 与 should 给它补上了一个 l。

items.en: Cunnan meant to know or to know how.
items.cn: cunnan 意为知道或懂得如何做。

items.en: Cuþe was the past form, meaning knew how.
items.cn: cuþe 是它的过去式，意为当时懂得如何做。

items.en: Coude carried the sense of past ability.
items.cn: coude 带着过去能力的意思继续使用。

items.en: An l was inserted to match would and should.
items.cn: 为了与 would、should 一致，词中插入了字母 l。

items.en: It now also marks possibility and polite requests.
items.cn: 今天它也用来表示可能性与礼貌请求。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers modals and one similar noun, and the meaning group names other modals of ability and possibility.
note.cn: 形近组收集情态动词与一个形近名词，近义组列出其他表示能力与可能的情态动词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a child in a tree, then move to lost keys and to a politely closed window.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从树上的孩子开始，再到找不到的钥匙，最后到一扇被礼貌关上的窗。

normal.en: Could is can wearing a past tense coat.
normal.cn: could 就是 can 披上一件过去时的外衣。

normal.en: The l is silent but it links could to would and should.
normal.cn: l 不发音，却把 could 与 would、should 连在一起。

normal.en: Could is softer than can, so requests sound lighter.
normal.cn: could 比 can 更软，所以请求听起来更轻。

normal.en: Could be means the door is open but nobody has walked in.
normal.cn: could be 表示门开着，但还没人走进来。

normal.en: Could have done points at a past that never happened.
normal.cn: could have done 指向一个从未发生的过去。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching a fruit one branch too high.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸向高出一截的果子。

abstract.en: Picture several doors open at once in a dark hall.
abstract.cn: 想象昏暗走廊里同时开着好几扇门。

abstract.en: Picture a request written in soft pencil, not ink.
abstract.cn: 想象一个用铅笔而不是墨水写下的请求。

examples.en: When I was young, I could climb that tree in seconds.
examples.cn: 我小时候几秒钟就能爬上那棵树。

examples.en: The keys could be in your coat.
examples.cn: 钥匙可能在你大衣里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 could 记成 can 的过去式加一个不发音的 l：能力退到过去，语气也变得温和。

root: 源自古英语 cunnan（知道、懂得如何做）的过去式 cuþe，中古英语作 coude，十六世纪仿 would、should 插入 l 定型。

sensesIntro.en: From strength remembered, to a possibility left open, and at last to a request made gentle.
sensesIntro.cn: 从记忆中的力气，到留着的可能性，最后到被放软的请求。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child reaching a high branch with ease.
core.cn: 核心意象：孩子轻松够到高高的树枝。

branches.en: Past strength is remembered as a fact.
branches.cn: 过去的力气被当作事实记住。

branches.en: One possible answer is left on the table.
branches.cn: 一种可能的答案被留在桌上。

branches.en: A request is offered with room to refuse.
branches.cn: 请求被提出时，还留着拒绝的余地。

branches.en: Both loosen certainty, one about the past and one about now.
branches.cn: 两者都放松了确定性，一个关于过去，一个关于现在。

branches.en: Possibility and politeness both keep a door slightly open.
branches.cn: 可能性与礼貌都把门留了一条缝。

intro.en: Could is a closed modal form; it changes for nothing and joins only with not or have.
intro.cn: could 是封闭的情态形式，本身不变形，只能与 not 或 have 组合。

latinIntro.en: The word is native English, not Latin, and keeps the old past ending.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是英语本族词，并非拉丁语，保留着古老的过去式词尾。

definition_zh: 委员会；理事会；地方议会；会议
definition_en: a group of people chosen to make decisions or give advice, especially for a town or organisation
core_image: 一张圆桌旁围坐着被推选出来的人，举手决定一件事
scene: 会议室里十二个人围坐一圈，举手表决是否修那条路。The city council voted to repair the old road.
sceneCN: 这里 council 指「地方议会」（第 2 个义项：管理城镇事务的议事机构）；句意是市议会投票决定修那条旧路。

pos.zh: 委员会；理事会；地方议会；会议

senses.title: A chosen decision group
senses.definition: a group of people chosen to make decisions or give advice
senses.definitionCN: 被推选出来做决定或提建议的一群人
senses.example: The arts council gave the theatre a grant.
senses.exampleCN: 艺术委员会给了这家剧院一笔拨款。
senses.why: Many voices need one table to become one decision.
senses.whyCN: 许多声音需要一张桌子，才能变成一个决定。

senses.title: The body that runs a town
senses.definition: the group that governs a town or local area
senses.definitionCN: 管理一座城镇或地方区域的机构
senses.example: The city council voted to repair the old road.
senses.exampleCN: 市议会投票决定修那条旧路。
senses.why: A town is too large for one desk, so it borrows a table of many.
senses.whyCN: 一座城一张桌子管不过来，于是借来一张多人的桌子。

senses.title: A meeting for advice
senses.definition: a formal meeting held to discuss and advise on a matter
senses.definitionCN: 为讨论并议定某事而召开的正式会议
senses.example: The generals held a council before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 将军们在黎明前开了一次军事会议。
senses.why: Before a hard act comes a room where words are weighed.
senses.whyCN: 艰难行动之前，总有一间称量话语的屋子。

intro.en: Council comes from Latin concilium, a calling together, from com-, together, and calare, to call.
intro.cn: council 来自拉丁语 concilium（召集到一起），由 com-（一起）与 calare（呼喊、召集）构成。

items.en: Calare meant to call or summon.
items.cn: calare 意为呼喊或召集。

items.en: Concilium named a body called together for advice.
items.cn: concilium 指为商议而被召集起来的团体。

items.en: Concile meant an assembly or a meeting.
items.cn: concile 意为集会或会议。

items.en: English council named a group that advises a ruler.
items.cn: 英语 council 指为统治者出主意的团体。

items.en: It now names town bodies, committees and formal meetings.
items.cn: 今天它指市政机构、委员会与正式会议。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the easily confused council, counsel and consul, and the meaning group names other decision groups.
note.cn: 形近组收集易混的 council、counsel 与 consul，近义组列出其他决策团体。

entries.definition: advice, or a lawyer who gives it
entries.definitionCN: 建议，或提供建议的律师

entries.definition: an official living abroad to help citizens
entries.definitionCN: 驻外帮助本国公民的官员

a small group chosen for a special task

entries.definition: the group that directs a company

entries.definitionCN: 为共同目的聚集的群体

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a round table of chosen people, then move to a town body and to generals meeting before dawn.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从被推选者的圆桌开始，再到市政机构，最后到黎明前开会的将军们。

normal.en: Council hides the word call: people called together to decide.
normal.cn: council 里藏着 call：被叫到一起做决定的人。

normal.en: Council is the group; counsel is the advice it gives.
normal.cn: council 是团体，counsel 是它给出的建议。

normal.en: A council sits at a round table so no seat looks highest.
normal.cn: 议会坐圆桌，这样没有哪个座位显得最高。

normal.en: City council decides roads, housing and rubbish.
normal.cn: 市议会决定道路、住房与垃圾的事。

normal.en: The ending -il is quiet, but the word means loud debate.
normal.cn: 词尾 -il 很安静，这个词的意思却是喧闹的辩论。

abstract.en: Picture many hands rising in a single room.
abstract.cn: 想象许多只手在同一间屋子里举起。

abstract.en: Picture a round table worn smooth by elbows.
abstract.cn: 想象一张被手肘磨得光滑的圆桌。

abstract.en: Picture a town seen from above as many doors and one table.
abstract.cn: 想象从高处看一座城，许多扇门和一张桌子。

examples.en: The city council voted to repair the old road.
examples.cn: 市议会投票决定修那条旧路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 council 记成「被 call 到一起的人」：被召集来议事的团体，就是委员会与议会。

root: 源自拉丁语 concilium（集会），由 com-（一起）与 calare（呼喊、召集）构成，本指被召集议事的人，后指委员会与地方议会。

sensesIntro.en: From a group called to advise, to the body that runs a town, and at last to the meeting itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被召来出主意的团体，到管理城镇的机构，最后到会议本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: chosen people seated around one round table.
core.cn: 核心意象：被推选的人围坐在一张圆桌旁。

branches.en: A chosen group turns talk into advice.
branches.cn: 被选出的团体把谈话变成建议。

branches.en: A town body turns advice into local rules.
branches.cn: 市政机构把建议变成地方规矩。

branches.en: A meeting turns many voices into one plan.
branches.cn: 一场会议把许多声音变成一个方案。

branches.en: Both are bodies with the power to decide.
branches.cn: 两者都是握有决定权的机构。

branches.en: The body and its meeting share one name because the meeting is the body at work.
branches.cn: 机构与会议共用一个名字，因为会议就是机构在工作。

intro.en: Council rests on Latin calare, to call, with com-, together, and the noun shape -ium.

latinIntro.en: The calling base cal- also appears in calendar and clamour.
latinIntro.cn: 表示呼喊与召集的词基 cal- 也出现在 calendar 与 clamour 中。

definition_en: to say numbers in order or find how many there are, to matter, or the total reached
core_image: 一只手指数过一排豆子，指尖一停就得出总数
scene: 孩子闭着眼，一只一只数着藏起来的小伙伴。She counted to ten before she opened her eyes.
sceneCN: 这里 count 指「数数」（第 1 个义项：按顺序说出数目）；句意是她数到十才睁开眼睛。

senses.title: To say numbers or find a total
senses.definition: to say numbers in order, or to find how many things there are
senses.definitionCN: 按顺序说出数字，或查明有多少个事物
senses.example: She counted to ten before she opened her eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 她数到十才睁开眼睛。
senses.why: A finger moving from object to object turns a crowd into a number.
senses.whyCN: 手指从一件东西移到另一件，人群就变成一个数。

senses.title: To matter
senses.definition: to have importance or value
senses.definitionCN: 具有重要性或价值
senses.example: Every vote counts in a small town.
senses.exampleCN: 在小镇上，每一票都重要。
senses.why: What is counted is noticed, and what is noticed has weight.
senses.whyCN: 被数到的东西才被看见，被看见的才有分量。

senses.title: The total reached
senses.definition: the number reached by counting, or the act of counting
senses.definitionCN: 数出来的数目，或数数这一行为
senses.example: The final count was three hundred.
senses.exampleCN: 最后的计数是三百。
senses.why: Counting ends by placing a single number on the table.
senses.whyCN: 数数最后，总要把一个数字放到桌上。

intro.en: Count comes from Latin computare, to reckon, through Old French conter, to tell or count.
intro.cn: count 来自拉丁语 computare（计算），经古法语 conter（讲述、计数）进入英语。

items.en: Computare meant to reckon or add up.
items.cn: computare 意为计算或合计。

items.en: Computus named a reckoning or an account.
items.cn: computus 指一次计算或一本账。

items.en: Conter meant to tell a story or count items.
items.cn: conter 意为讲述故事或清点物品。

items.en: English count named the act of numbering.
items.cn: 英语 count 指数数这一动作。

items.en: It also means to matter, as in every second counts.
items.cn: 它也表示重要，如 every second counts。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words near count in shape, and the meaning group names other words for numbering and mattering.
note.cn: 形近组收集形状接近 count 的词，近义组列出其他表示计数与重要的说法。

abstract.en: Picture a total written at the bottom of a long page.

examples.en: She counted to ten before she opened her eyes.

senses.why: A state is too large to know every farm, so it is cut into counties.
senses.whyCN: 一个州大到认不清每座农场，只好切成一个个县。

senses.title: A shire in Britain
senses.definition: a local government area in Britain, Ireland or Canada
senses.definitionCN: 英国、爱尔兰或加拿大的地方行政区
senses.example: Yorkshire is a large county in the north of England.
senses.exampleCN: 约克郡是英格兰北部一个大郡。
senses.why: Britain keeps the old lands that a lord once held.
senses.whyCN: 英国保留了旧时由领主掌管的那片土地。

senses.title: The people of a county
senses.definition: the people or the government of such an area, treated as one body
senses.definitionCN: 这样一个地区的居民或政府，被视为一个整体
senses.example: The county voted for a new library.
senses.exampleCN: 全县投票支持建一座新图书馆。
senses.why: Land and people share one name, so a county can speak with one voice.
senses.whyCN: 土地和人共用一个名字，所以一个县能用同一个声音说话。

intro.en: County comes from Latin comes, a companion, through Old French conte, a count, and comitatus, his land.
intro.cn: county 源自拉丁语 comes（同伴），经古法语 conte（伯爵）与拉丁语 comitatus（伯爵的领地）进入英语。

items.en: Comes meant a companion, often a man at court.
items.cn: comes 意为同伴，常指宫廷中随侍的人。

items.en: Comitatus named the land under a count.
items.cn: comitatus 指一位伯爵管辖的领地。

items.en: Conte named a count, a noble lord.
items.cn: conte 指伯爵，即一位贵族领主。

items.en: Counte first named the land a count ruled.
items.cn: counte 最初指伯爵所治理的土地。

items.en: It now names a local district in many countries.
items.cn: 今天它指许多国家里的地方行政区。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the count spelling, and the meaning group names other units of local land.
note.cn: 形近组共享 count 这个拼写，近义组列出其他表示地方行政区域的说法。

entries.definition: a nation or its rural land
to add up numbers in order
a record of money paid and owed
an area marked off for local government
entries.definitionCN: 为地方管理划出的一片区域

entries.definition: a large region under one government
entries.definitionCN: 归同一政府管辖的大区域

entries.definition: an old English county

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a count and his land, then move to a map of small squares.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一位伯爵和他的领地开始，再到一张切成小方格的地图。

normal.en: County hides the word count: the land a count once ruled.
normal.cn: county 里藏着 count：一位伯爵当年治理的地。

normal.en: A county is a slice of a state, thin enough to govern.
normal.cn: 县是州切下的一片，薄到足以治理。

normal.en: Every county on the map has a seat where the laws sit.
normal.cn: 地图上每个县都有一个安放法令的县城。

normal.en: The county fixes the roads you drive on every day.
normal.cn: 你每天开车经过的路，由县里来修。

normal.en: When the whole county votes, one voice carries far.
normal.cn: 全县投票时，一个声音能传得很远。

abstract.en: Picture a map ruled into squares by thin grey lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图被细灰线划成方格。

abstract.en: Picture a stone courthouse at the centre of those lines.
abstract.cn: 想象那些线中心的一座石造法院。

abstract.en: Picture a single road sign naming the county as you enter.
abstract.cn: 想象你驶入时那块写着县名的路牌。

examples.en: He works for the county as a road engineer.
examples.cn: 他在县里当道路工程师。

examples.en: The river marks the border between the two counties.
examples.cn: 这条河是两个县之间的界线。

examples.en: Our county is famous for its apples.
examples.cn: 我们县以苹果闻名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 county 记成 count（伯爵）加 y：伯爵管的那片地，就是郡，再小一级就是县。

root: 源自拉丁语 comes（同伴、侍从），经古法语 conte（伯爵）与晚期拉丁语 comitatus（伯爵领地）进入英语，本指伯爵管辖之地，后成为县、郡一类行政区。

sensesIntro.en: From a count's land to a state district to the whole body of people living there.
sensesIntro.cn: 从伯爵的领地，到州以下的行政区，最后到住在其中的全体居民。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a map cut into squares, each with a name.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张被切成方格的地图，每格写着名字。

branches.en: A state is sliced into counties so each piece can be governed.
branches.cn: 州被切成一个个县，每片都能被治理。

branches.en: Britain keeps the older name for the same kind of land.
branches.cn: 英国用更古老的名字称呼同一种土地。

branches.en: The people inside the lines can vote and speak together.
branches.cn: 界内的居民能一起投票、一起发声。

branches.en: A county is both a piece of land and the body of people on it.
branches.cn: 县既是土地的一片，也是其上人群的整体。

branches.en: The old shire and its people still share one name.
branches.cn: 古老的郡与它的居民仍共用一个名字。

intro.en: County pairs the count base with the place ending -y, and grows a small family of compounds.
intro.cn: county 把 count 词基与表地点的词尾 -y 结合，又长出少量复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base comitatus, a count's land, still lies under the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 comitatus（伯爵领地）至今仍垫在这个词下面。

items.meaningCN: 归地方管理的一片区域
items.example: The county is small but busy.

items.exampleCN: 他们做了一次全县调查。

items.meaning: a person who lives in a county
items.example: Every countian knows the old bridge.
items.exampleCN: 每个县民都认得那座老桥。

items.meaning: a noble lord in old Europe
items.exampleCN: 那位伯爵拥有三个村庄。

items.example: They gave us a small discount.
items.exampleCN: 他们给了我们一点折扣。

definition_en: two people or things that go together, or to join two things
core_image: 两只手在桌子底下悄悄握在一起
scene: 雨里只有一把伞，两个人紧挨着走过马路。The couple shared one umbrella across the street.
sceneCN: 这里 couple 指「情侣」（第 2 个义项：成对相伴的两个人）；句意是那对情侣共撑一把伞过街。

senses.title: Two of a kind together
senses.definition: two people or things of the same kind that go together
senses.definitionCN: 同类的两个被放在一起的人或物
senses.example: I bought a couple of chairs for the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 我买了两把厨房用的椅子。
senses.why: Two things that belong together make one small team.
senses.whyCN: 两个彼此相属的东西，就组成一个小小的组合。

senses.title: Two people in love
senses.definition: two people who are married or in a romantic relationship
senses.definitionCN: 结了婚或处在恋爱关系中的两个人
senses.example: The couple moved in last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这对情侣去年春天搬了进来。
senses.why: Love turns two separate lives into one pair.
senses.whyCN: 爱情把两段各自的生活变成一双。

senses.title: To join two things
senses.definition: to join two things or ideas together
senses.definitionCN: 把两个事物或想法接在一起
senses.example: The engineer coupled the two pipes.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师把两根管子接了起来。
senses.why: Two ends meet and become one line.
senses.whyCN: 两个端点相接，就成了一条线。

intro.en: Couple comes from Latin copula, a bond, built from co-, together, and apere, to fasten.
intro.cn: couple 源自拉丁语 copula（纽带），由 co-（共同）与 apere（系上）构成。

items.en: Copula meant a band that ties two things.
items.cn: copula 意为把两样东西系住的带子。

items.en: Copulare meant to fasten things together.
items.cn: copulare 意为把东西系在一起。

items.en: Cople named a pair joined by a bond.
items.cn: cople 指被一条纽带系在一起的一对。

items.en: Couple first meant two things tied as one.
items.cn: couple 最初指被系成一体的两样东西。

items.en: It now names pairs of people as well as the act of joining.
items.cn: 今天它既指成对的人，也指连接这个动作。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the coup- shape, and the meaning group names other words for two things together.
note.cn: 形近组共享 coup- 这一词形，近义组列出其他表示「两个一起」的说法。

entries.definition: a device that joins two parts
entries.definitionCN: 把两个部件连起来的装置

entries.definition: two lines of poetry that rhyme
to hold someone close with care
two things of the same kind used together
two people who perform together
one of two people in a shared activity
entries.definitionCN: 共同活动中的两个人之一

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with one bond tying two things, then move to a pair in love and to pipes joined.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一根纽带系住两样东西开始，再到相爱的一对，最后到接起来的两根管子。

normal.en: A couple is two things held by one invisible band.
normal.cn: 一对就是被一条看不见的带子系住的两样东西。

normal.en: One umbrella and two shoulders: the picture of a couple.
normal.cn: 一把伞、两个肩膀，就是一对的样子。

normal.en: Say a couple of minutes and you mean two or three.
normal.cn: 说 a couple of minutes，意思就是两三分钟。

normal.en: To couple pipes is to let two ends kiss.
normal.cn: 把管子接起来，就是让两个端口相碰。

normal.en: A couple on a train ticket means one seat for two names.
normal.cn: 车票上的两个人，意味着两个名字共用一个座位。

abstract.en: Picture two rings linked through each other.
abstract.cn: 想象两枚戒指互相套住。

abstract.en: Picture two hands that refuse to let go.
abstract.cn: 想象两只不肯松开的手。

abstract.en: Picture one knot joining two short ropes.
abstract.cn: 想象一个结把两根短绳连成一根。

examples.en: A couple of students waited outside the office.
examples.cn: 两个学生在办公室外等着。

examples.en: The couple walked home along the river.
examples.cn: 这对情侣沿着河走回家。

examples.en: The wagon was coupled to the engine.
examples.cn: 车厢被挂到了火车头上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 couple 记成 copula（纽带）的同胞：一根带子把两个人系在一起，就是一对。

root: 源自拉丁语 copula（纽带、联结），由 co-（共同）与 apere（系上）构成，本指把两物系在一起之物，后指成对的人或物，也指连接这个动作。

sensesIntro.en: From two things tied by a bond, to two people in love, to the act of joining itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被纽带系住的两样东西，到相爱的一对，最后到连接这个动作本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one short band holding two objects.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条短带子把两个东西系在一起。

branches.en: Two things of a kind are tied into one small unit.
branches.cn: 同类的两个东西被系成一个小单位。

branches.en: Two people become a pair that others see as one.
branches.cn: 两个人成为别人眼中的一体。

branches.en: The verb keeps the old picture of a bond pulled tight.
branches.cn: 动词义保留了把纽带拉紧的旧画面。

branches.en: A pair is the result, coupling is the act.
branches.cn: 一对是结果，连接是动作。

branches.en: Love is a bond that people tie and keep.
branches.cn: 爱情就是人们自己系上并留住的纽带。

intro.en: Couple is a base word from Latin copula, extended by endings that mark pairs, joining and tools.
intro.cn: couple 是源自拉丁语 copula 的词根词，再由表示成对、连接与工具的各类词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: The bond base cop- still appears in copula and in the grammar term copular.
latinIntro.cn: 表示纽带的词基 cop- 仍出现在 copula 与语法术语 copular 中。

items.exampleCN: 三对伴侣共用一张桌子。

items.meaning: the act or part that joins
items.example: The coupling broke in the cold.

items.meaning: a device that joins two parts

items.example: The poem ends with a couplet.
items.exampleCN: 这首诗以一副对句结尾。

items.meaning: a linking word such as be
items.meaningCN: 像 be 这样的系动词
items.example: The copula links subject and noun.
items.exampleCN: 系动词连接主语与名词。

definition_en: the ability to face danger or pain without letting fear stop you
core_image: 一个人腿在发抖，还是向前迈出了一步
scene: 火警响起，他还是冲进屋里抱出了孩子。It took courage to run into the burning house.
sceneCN: 这里 courage 指「勇气」（第 1 个义项：面对危险仍向前的能力）；句意是冲进着火的房子需要勇气。

senses.title: Strength before danger
senses.definition: the ability to face danger or pain without letting fear stop you
senses.definitionCN: 面对危险或痛苦时不被恐惧挡住的力量
senses.example: It took courage to enter the dark cave.
senses.exampleCN: 走进那个黑漆漆的山洞需要勇气。
senses.why: Fear shouts stop, and courage takes one more step.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧喊着停下，勇气却再迈一步。

senses.title: Strength to do what is hard
senses.definition: the strength to do something difficult or unpopular
senses.definitionCN: 去做困难或不受欢迎之事的力量
senses.example: She had the courage to say no.
senses.exampleCN: 她有胆量说不。
senses.why: Saying no to a crowd needs a voice of your own.
senses.whyCN: 对着一群人说「不」，需要有自己的声音。

senses.title: A steady inner confidence
senses.definition: a feeling of confidence that lets a person try
senses.definitionCN: 让人敢于尝试的一种内在信心
senses.example: The good news gave him courage.
senses.exampleCN: 这个好消息给了他底气。
senses.why: A little proof can turn doubt into a steady breath.
senses.whyCN: 一点点证明，就能把疑虑变成平稳的呼吸。

intro.en: Courage goes back to Latin cor, the heart, through Old French corage, the heart as the seat of brave feeling.
intro.cn: courage 可追溯到拉丁语 cor（心），经古法语 corage（作为勇敢之情所在的心）进入英语。

items.en: Cor meant the heart and the feelings seated there.
items.cn: cor 意为心，以及安放在心里的情感。

items.en: Coraticum named the feelings that rise from the heart.
items.cn: coraticum 指从心里升起的情绪。

items.en: Corage meant the heart as the source of brave feeling.
items.cn: corage 指作为勇敢之情来源的心。

items.en: Courage first meant the heart and its moods.
items.cn: courage 最初指心以及心的各种状态。

items.en: It now names the strength to meet danger.
items.cn: 今天它专指迎接危险的那股力量。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same courage base, and the meaning group names other words for boldness.
note.cn: 形近组收集建立在 courage 词基上的词，近义组列出其他表示勇敢的说法。

entries.definition: to give someone hope and support
to take away someone's confidence
showing no fear when there is danger
the quality of facing danger without fear
entries.definitionCN: 面对危险不畏惧的品质

entries.definition: the cool boldness to do a hard thing
the willingness to take a risk

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a beating heart, then move to a voice that says no and to a steady breath.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一颗跳动的心开始，再到一个敢说「不」的声音，最后到平稳的呼吸。

normal.en: Courage holds the Latin word for heart, cor.
normal.cn: courage 里藏着拉丁语的心，cor。

normal.en: Fear is loud, but courage is the step you take anyway.
normal.cn: 恐惧很响，勇气是你照样迈出的那一步。

normal.en: A person of courage feels fear first and moves after.
normal.cn: 有勇气的人先感到害怕，然后才动。

normal.en: Moral courage is saying no when everyone nods.
normal.cn: 道德勇气就是众人都点头时你说不。

normal.en: One kind word can hand someone else your courage.
normal.cn: 一句好话就能把你的勇气递到别人手里。

abstract.en: Picture a small flame that refuses to go out in wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一小簇在风里也不肯熄灭的火。

abstract.en: Picture a foot lifted while the whole body shakes.
abstract.cn: 想象全身发抖时仍抬起的一只脚。

abstract.en: Picture a door opened onto a dark room.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门朝黑屋子被推开。

examples.en: It takes courage to admit a mistake.
examples.cn: 承认错误需要勇气。

examples.en: She found the courage to speak in front of the class.
examples.cn: 她鼓起勇气在全班面前发言。

examples.en: His courage during the flood saved two families.
examples.cn: 他在洪水中的勇气救了两家人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 courage 记成 cor（心）加 age：心里憋着的那股劲儿，就是勇气。

root: 源自拉丁语 cor（心），经古法语 corage 进入英语，本指心以及心的情感，后专指面对危险时从心里生出的力量。

sensesIntro.en: From the heart in danger, to the voice that refuses, to the quiet confidence that remains.
sensesIntro.cn: 从危险中的那颗心，到敢于拒绝的声音，最后到留下的那份安静的底气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shaking leg taking one firm step forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：发抖的腿向前迈出坚定的一步。

branches.en: The body wants to run and the heart decides to stay.
branches.cn: 身体想逃，心却决定留下。

branches.en: Doing the hard right thing needs a voice of your own.
branches.cn: 去做艰难而正确的事，需要有自己的声音。

branches.en: Confidence grows when someone believes in you.
branches.cn: 有人相信你时，底气就长出来。

branches.en: Both danger and disapproval test the same heart.
branches.cn: 危险与反对考验的是同一颗心。

branches.en: A steady heart can both refuse and begin.
branches.cn: 一颗稳的心既能拒绝，也能开始。

intro.en: Courage is built on the heart base cour-, which grows verbs with en- and dis- and adjectives with -ous.
intro.cn: courage 建立在表示心的词基 cour- 上，再由 en- 与 dis- 造动词，用 -ous 造形容词。

latinIntro.en: The heart base cor still beats inside courage, cordial and record.
latinIntro.cn: 表示心的词基 cor 仍跳动在 courage、cordial 与 record 里。

items.example: A courageous driver stopped the bus.
items.exampleCN: 一位勇敢的司机把车停住了。
她的鼓励让我坚持下去。

definition_en: a series of lessons, the way something develops, or one part of a meal
core_image: 一条跑道从脚下一直伸到看不见的远处
scene: 新生拿着课表在教学楼里找自己那门课。She signed up for a course in Italian cooking.
sceneCN: 这里 course 指「课程」（第 1 个义项：一系列有安排的课）；句意是她报名了一门意大利烹饪课。

senses.title: A set of lessons
senses.definition: a series of lessons on one subject
senses.definitionCN: 围绕一个科目安排的一系列课
senses.example: She is taking a course in French.
senses.exampleCN: 她正在修一门法语课。
senses.why: Learning is a road with a set number of steps.
senses.whyCN: 学习就是一条设有固定步数的路。

senses.title: The way time runs
senses.definition: the way something develops over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 事物在一段时间里发展的方式
senses.example: In the course of the year the town changed.
senses.exampleCN: 在这一年里，这座小镇变了。
senses.why: Time runs like water and marks its own channel.
senses.whyCN: 时间像水一样奔流，并留下自己的河道。

senses.title: One part of a meal
senses.definition: one of the parts of a meal, served separately
senses.definitionCN: 一餐中单独上桌的其中一道
senses.example: The main course was fish.
senses.exampleCN: 主菜是鱼。
senses.why: A meal is served in stages, like a road in stretches.
senses.whyCN: 一顿饭分段上桌，就像一条路分成几段。

intro.en: Course comes from Latin cursus, a running or a race, from currere, to run.
intro.cn: course 源自拉丁语 cursus（奔跑、赛跑），来自动词 currere（跑）。

items.en: Cursus meant a running or a race.
items.cn: cursus 意为奔跑或赛跑。

items.en: Currere meant to run quickly.
items.cn: currere 意为快速奔跑。

items.en: Cours named the path a river or a race follows.
items.cn: cours 指河流或赛跑所循的路线。

items.en: Course first meant the way something runs.
items.cn: course 最初指事物奔行的方式。

items.en: It now covers lessons, meals and the passage of time.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖课程、菜式与时间的流逝。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words that sound like course, and the meaning group names other words for a path or a lesson.
note.cn: 形近组收集与 course 读音相近的短词，近义组列出其他表示路线与课程的说法。

a wish that harm will come to someone
the reason why something happens
a period of teaching one subject
entries.definitionCN: 教授某个科目的一节课

entries.definition: the way from one place to another
entries.definitionCN: 从一地到另一地的走法

entries.definition: a series of changes that lead to a result
entries.definitionCN: 通向结果的一系列变化

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a running track, then move to time flowing and to a dish carried in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一条跑道开始，再到流动的时间，最后到端上桌的一道菜。

normal.en: Course comes from a word for running, so every course is a track.
normal.cn: course 来自表示奔跑的词，所以每一门课都是一条跑道。

normal.en: A course of study has a start, a middle and a finish line.
normal.cn: 一门课程有起点、中间和终点线。

normal.en: In the course of a day, the sun draws the same arc.
normal.cn: 一天的过程里，太阳画出同一道弧。

normal.en: The main course arrives when the road of dinner is halfway.
normal.cn: 主菜上来时，晚餐这条路正好走到一半。

normal.en: Of course means the road is clear: no doubt at all.
normal.cn: of course 表示路很清楚：毫无疑问。

abstract.en: Picture a river cutting its own channel through soil.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河在泥土里切出自己的河道。

abstract.en: Picture footprints in a straight line across a field.
abstract.cn: 想象田野上一串笔直的脚印。

abstract.en: Picture plates arriving one after another on a table.
abstract.cn: 想象盘子一个接一个端上桌。

examples.en: The course lasts twelve weeks.
examples.cn: 这门课持续十二周。

examples.en: In the course of the meeting she said nothing.
examples.cn: 会议进行过程中她一言未发。

examples.en: We had soup, then a fish course.
examples.cn: 我们喝了汤，然后上了一道鱼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 course 记成 cur（跑）加 se：一条被人跑出来的路，既是路线，也是要走完的课程。

root: 源自拉丁语 cursus（奔跑、跑道），来自动词 currere（跑），经古法语 cours 进入英语，本指跑出的路线，后引申为过程、课程与一餐中的一道菜。

sensesIntro.en: From a track that is run, to the flow of time, to one stage of a meal.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被跑过的跑道，到时间的流动，最后到一餐中的一个阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a track running from the feet to the horizon.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条从脚下伸向天边的跑道。

branches.en: A course of lessons is a track with numbered steps.
branches.cn: 一门课程就是标好步数的跑道。

branches.en: Time runs forward and leaves a channel behind.
branches.cn: 时间向前奔流，留下一条河道。

branches.en: A meal moves in stages, each one a short stretch.
branches.cn: 一餐分阶段推进，每一段都不长。

branches.en: Both a lesson plan and a life have a course to finish.
branches.cn: 课程表与人生都有一条要走完的路。

branches.en: From the flow of time to the order of dishes, sequence rules.
branches.cn: 从时间的流动到菜的顺序，都是先后在起作用。

intro.en: Course is built on the Latin running base curs-, which also gives current, courier and excursion.
intro.cn: course 建立在拉丁语表示奔跑的词基 curs- 上，current、courier 与 excursion 也由它构成。

latinIntro.en: The running base curr- still runs through current, courier and occur.
latinIntro.cn: 表示奔跑的词基 curr- 至今仍贯穿 current、courier 与 occur。

items.example: The course is open to all.
Blood was coursing through his veins.
Coursework counts for half the mark.

items.meaning: a book used in a course
items.example: Open your coursebook to page ten.
The current pulled the boat away.

items.meaning: a person who runs with messages
items.exampleCN: 一名快递员送来了包裹。

definition_en: a place where legal cases are judged, an area for a ball game, or the home of a king
core_image: 高背木椅后挂着国徽，椅子下方站着两排人
scene: 法官敲下小锤，庭下所有人立刻安静下来。The whole court waited for the judge to speak.
sceneCN: 这里 court 指「法院」（第 1 个义项：审理案件的场所）；句意是整个法庭都在等法官开口。

senses.title: The room of law
senses.definition: a place where legal cases are heard and judged
senses.definitionCN: 审理并判决法律案件的场所
senses.example: The case will come to court next month.
senses.exampleCN: 这个案子下个月开庭。
senses.why: When two sides cannot agree, they bring the quarrel to one room.
senses.whyCN: 当两边谈不拢，就把争执搬进同一间屋子。

senses.title: The ground for a game
senses.definition: an area marked out for a ball game
senses.definitionCN: 为球类运动划出的场地
senses.example: They booked a tennis court for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 他们订了一小时网球场。
senses.why: A game needs lines before it can have rules.
senses.whyCN: 比赛先要有线，才谈得上规则。

senses.title: The house of a king
senses.definition: the home and household of a king or queen
senses.definitionCN: 国王或女王的居所与随从群体
senses.example: The young prince grew up at court.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻的王子在宫廷里长大。
senses.why: Power always gathers around one seat.
senses.whyCN: 权力总要聚到同一把椅子周围。

intro.en: Court comes from Latin cohors, an enclosed yard and the guard around a leader, through Old French cort.
intro.cn: court 源自拉丁语 cohors（围起的院子、首领身边的卫队），经古法语 cort 进入英语。

items.en: Cohors meant an enclosed yard or a band of soldiers.
items.cn: cohors 意为围起的院子或一队士兵。

items.en: The word named both the yard and the guard around a leader.
items.cn: 这个词同时指院子和围绕首领的卫队。

items.en: Cort named the yard of a castle and the lord's household.
items.cn: cort 指城堡的院子和领主的家眷随从。

items.en: Court first meant the yard where a lord lived.
items.cn: court 最初指领主居住的院落。

items.en: It now names law courts, ball courts and royal households.
items.cn: 今天它指法院、球场与王室宫廷。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words close in sound, and the meaning group names places of judgement, enclosure and rule.
note.cn: 形近组收集读音接近的短词，近义组列出与审判、围合和统治有关的场所。

entries.definition: a unit of liquid equal to two pints
entries.definitionCN: 等于两品脱的液体单位

entries.definition: short in a way that seems rude
a piece of clothing worn over other clothes
entries.definitionCN: 穿在其他衣服外面的外套

entries.definition: a body that judges special cases
an enclosed area beside a building
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物旁边的围起空地

entries.definition: the large official home of a ruler
entries.definitionCN: 统治者居住的宏大官邸

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a yard behind a wall, then move to a judge and to a game on marked ground.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从墙后的一处院子开始，再到一位法官，最后到划好线的比赛场地。

normal.en: A court was first a yard: four walls around some ground.
normal.cn: court 最初就是院子：四面墙围住一块地。

normal.en: The same walls now hold a judge instead of a lord.
normal.cn: 同样的墙里如今坐着法官，而不是领主。

normal.en: A tennis court is just an empty yard with white lines.
normal.cn: 网球场不过是一个画了白线的空院子。

normal.en: To court someone is to stand in their yard and hope.
normal.cn: 追求一个人，就是站在人家院外满心期待。

normal.en: At court, everyone watches the one chair.
normal.cn: 在宫廷里，所有人都盯着那把椅子。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden hammer coming down on a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一把木锤落在桌面上。

abstract.en: Picture white lines painted on red ground.
abstract.cn: 想象红地上画出的白线。

abstract.en: Picture a row of tall chairs facing one taller chair.
abstract.cn: 想象一排高椅朝着一把更高的椅子。

examples.en: The court found him not guilty.
examples.cn: 法庭判他无罪。

examples.en: They play basketball on the court behind the school.
examples.cn: 他们在学校后面的球场上打篮球。

examples.en: The queen held court in the great hall.
examples.cn: 女王在大厅里接受朝见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 court 记成「考他」：把人带上法庭考问一番，院子就成了审案的地方。

root: 源自拉丁语 cohors（围起的院子、首领的卫队），经古法语 cort 进入英语，本指领主的院落与随从，后指宫廷、法庭与球场。

sensesIntro.en: From an enclosed yard to the room of law, the marked ground of a game and the seat of a king.
sensesIntro.cn: 从围起的院子，到审案的屋子、划线的球场，最后到国王的居所。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: four walls closing around a piece of open ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：四面墙围住一块空地。

branches.en: The enclosed yard becomes the room where law is spoken.
branches.cn: 围起的院子变成宣读法律的那间屋子。

branches.en: The same enclosed ground is marked out for a game.
branches.cn: 同样的围合空地被划线用来比赛。

branches.en: A ruler keeps a court of guards, clerks and suppliants.
branches.cn: 统治者身边聚着卫兵、文书与求见者。

branches.en: Both are bounded spaces where rules decide what counts.
branches.cn: 两者都是规则说了算的边界之内。

branches.en: Games and power both draw a crowd of watchers.
branches.cn: 比赛与权力都会招来一圈旁观者。

intro.en: Court is a base word from Latin cohors, extended by endings and by compounds with room, house and yard.
intro.cn: court 是源自拉丁语 cohors 的词根词，再由词尾和与 room、house、yard 的复合法扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin yard base cohort- also appears in cohort, a group of soldiers.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示院子的词基 cohort- 也出现在 cohort（一队士兵）里。

items.meaning: an enclosed place of law or play
items.meaningCN: 围起来的审案或比赛场所

items.example: He courted her for a year.

items.meaning: the act of seeking love or favour
items.meaningCN: 求爱或求取好感的行为
items.exampleCN: 他们的恋爱持续了一个夏天。

items.meaning: polite in the manner of a court
items.meaningCN: 有宫廷风度的，彬彬有礼的
items.exampleCN: 他行了一个宫廷式的礼。

items.meaning: the room where cases are heard

items.example: The courthouse stands on the square.

definition_zh: 堂兄弟姐妹；表兄弟姐妹；远亲
definition_en: a child of your uncle or aunt, or a distant relative
core_image: 过年时一屋子小孩被大人按辈分排成一排
scene: 过年时她被妈妈推到一个陌生男孩面前，说这是你表哥。She met her cousin for the first time at the family dinner.
sceneCN: 这里 cousin 指「表兄弟姐妹」（第 1 个义项：姑舅姨的孩子）；句意是她在家庭聚餐上第一次见到表兄。

pos.zh: 堂兄弟姐妹；表兄弟姐妹；远亲

collocations.phrase: a cousin on my mother's side

senses.title: A child of your uncle
senses.definition: the child of your uncle or aunt
senses.definitionCN: 你叔叔、舅舅、姑母或姨母的孩子
senses.example: My cousin lives in the next town.
senses.exampleCN: 我表哥住在邻镇。
senses.why: Two families branch out from the same trunk.
senses.whyCN: 两个家庭从同一根树干上分出来。

senses.title: A relative far up the tree
senses.definition: any relative who is not close but shares an ancestor
senses.definitionCN: 关系不近、但共有一位祖先的亲戚
senses.example: He is a distant cousin of the painter.
senses.exampleCN: 他是那位画家的远房亲戚。
senses.why: The family tree keeps branching long after the names fade.
senses.whyCN: 名字都记不清了，家谱还在继续分叉。

intro.en: Cousin comes from Latin consobrinus, the child of a mother's sister, through Old French cosin.
intro.cn: cousin 源自拉丁语 consobrinus（姨母的孩子），经古法语 cosin 进入英语。

items.en: Consobrinus named the child of a mother's sister.
items.cn: consobrinus 指母亲姐妹的孩子。

items.en: Com- together and sobrinus cousin built the word.
items.cn: com-（共同）与 sobrinus（表亲）合成了这个词。

items.en: Cosin widened the sense to any uncle's child.
items.cn: cosin 把意思扩大到任何叔伯姑舅姨的孩子。

items.en: Cousin entered English with that wider sense.
items.cn: cousin 带着这个更宽的意思进入英语。

items.en: It now also covers relatives far out on the family tree.
items.cn: 今天它还包括家谱上关系很远的亲戚。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words close in sound to cousin, and the meaning group names other family words.
note.cn: 形近组收集与 cousin 读音接近的词，近义组列出其他亲属称谓。

entries.definition: to trick someone for money
a soft pad to sit or rest on
a function used in trigonometry
entries.definitionCN: 三角学中使用的一种函数

entries.definition: a person connected to you by family
a male relative of your blood
entries.definitionCN: 有血缘关系的男性亲属

entries.definition: the son of your brother or sister

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with children of two brothers, then move to a tree that keeps branching.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两兄弟的孩子开始，再到一棵不断分叉的家谱树。

normal.en: Two brothers start two families, and their children are cousins.
normal.cn: 两兄弟开两支家，他们的孩子就是表亲。

normal.en: A cousin is a brother with a different address.
normal.cn: 表兄弟就是住在另一个地址的兄弟。

normal.en: At the family dinner, cousin is the name for the child you do not know yet.
normal.cn: 在家宴上，cousin 就是你还没认熟的那个孩子。

normal.en: Climb high enough on the tree and everyone becomes a cousin.
normal.cn: 在家谱上爬得够高，人人都成了亲戚。

normal.en: A distant cousin shares a great grandparent and little else.
normal.cn: 远房亲戚只共一位曾祖，别的几乎不共。

abstract.en: Picture two branches leaving one thick trunk.
abstract.cn: 想象两根枝条从同一根粗树干分出去。

abstract.en: Picture two children pushed together by grown hands.
abstract.cn: 想象两个小孩被大人的手推到一起。

abstract.en: Picture a family tree fading at its far edges.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵家谱树在远端渐渐模糊。

examples.en: My cousin taught me to swim.
examples.cn: 我表哥教会了我游泳。

examples.en: All my cousins came to the wedding.
examples.cn: 我的表亲们都来参加了婚礼。

examples.en: She is a cousin on my father's side.
examples.cn: 她是我父亲那边的表亲。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cousin 记成 co（共同）加 sin（同一血脉）：共着一份血脉的人，就是堂表亲。

root: 源自拉丁语 consobrinus（姨母的孩子），由 com-（共同）与 sobrinus（表亲）构成，经古法语 cosin 进入英语，泛指叔伯姑舅姨的孩子，也指远亲。

sensesIntro.en: From the child of an uncle or aunt to any relative far out on the family tree.
sensesIntro.cn: 从叔伯姑舅姨的孩子，到家谱上关系很远的所有亲戚。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two branches leaving the same family trunk.
core.cn: 核心意象：两根枝条从同一根家谱树干分出。

branches.en: The children of two siblings are cousins to each other.
branches.cn: 两个兄弟姐妹的孩子彼此是堂表亲。

branches.en: Far up the tree, the shared ancestor is the only link.
branches.cn: 在家谱高处，共有的祖先成了唯一联系。

branches.en: Both senses rest on one ancestor and two family lines.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在一位祖先与两条家系上。

branches.en: The near cousin is met at dinners and holidays.
branches.cn: 近亲常在饭桌和节日上见面。

branches.en: The far cousin may be known only from a story.
branches.cn: 远房亲戚也许只从故事里听说过。

intro.en: Cousin is a French borrowing whose family is built with the endings -ly and -hood.
intro.cn: cousin 是来自法语的借词，它的词族靠 -ly 与 -hood 等词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base consobrinus, a mother's sister's child, lies under the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 consobrinus（姨母的孩子）垫在这个词下面。

items.meaning: a child of an uncle or aunt

items.meaningCN: 像表亲之间那样亲热的
items.exampleCN: 他们之间有一种表亲般的情谊。
他们的表亲关系持续了一生。

items.meaning: the child of an aunt or uncle
a cousin one generation further out
items.example: A second cousin wrote to us.
items.exampleCN: 一位远房表亲写信给我们。

items.meaning: a cousin far out on the tree
items.meaningCN: 家谱上关系很远的亲戚
items.example: A distant cousin owns the farm.
items.exampleCN: 一位远亲拥有那座农场。

items.meaning: an old phrase for a first cousin
items.example: The will named a cousin german.
items.exampleCN: 遗嘱里提到一位嫡亲表亲。

definition_en: to put something over another thing, to include, or the front of a book
core_image: 一块布被抖开，盖住桌上的所有东西
scene: 天要下雨，她抓起一块塑料布把整堆柴火盖住。She used a cloth to cover the bread on the table.
sceneCN: 这里 cover 指「覆盖」（第 1 个义项：把东西盖在上面）；句意是她用一块布盖住了桌上的面包。

senses.title: To lay something over
senses.definition: to put something over a thing so that it is hidden or protected
senses.definitionCN: 把东西盖在另一物上，使它被遮住或受保护
senses.example: She covered the bread with a cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一块布盖住了面包。
senses.why: A cover is a second skin laid over the first.
senses.whyCN: 覆盖物就是披在原来那层皮上的第二层皮。

senses.title: To include a whole range
senses.definition: to include a subject, an area or a cost
senses.definitionCN: 把某个主题、区域或费用包含在内
senses.example: The book covers the whole history of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书涵盖了这座城市全部的历史。
senses.why: A wide cloth thrown over many objects holds them all.
senses.whyCN: 一块大布盖在许多东西上，就把它们全兜住了。

senses.title: The front of a book
senses.definition: the outer front part of a book or a magazine
senses.definitionCN: 书或杂志最外面的正面部分
senses.example: The cover shows a blue mountain.
senses.exampleCN: 封面画的是一座蓝色的山。
senses.why: The first thing you see is the cloth over the contents.
senses.whyCN: 你最先看到的，是盖在内容外面的那块布。

intro.en: Cover comes from Latin cooperire, to hide completely, built from co-, wholly, and operire, to shut.
intro.cn: cover 源自拉丁语 cooperire（完全遮住），由 co-（全然）与 operire（关上）构成。

items.en: Operire meant to shut or to hide something.
items.cn: operire 意为关上或遮住某物。

items.en: Cooperire meant to hide a thing all over.
items.cn: cooperire 意为把一物整个盖住。

items.en: Covrir meant to put something over a thing.
items.cn: covrir 意为把东西盖在上面。

items.en: Cover first meant to protect something with a layer.
items.cn: cover 最初指用一层东西保护某物。

items.en: It now also means to report, to include and to pay for.
items.cn: 今天它也表示报道、涵盖与支付。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words near cover in shape, and the meaning group names other ways of hiding or shielding.
note.cn: 形近组收集与 cover 形状接近的短词，近义组列出其他遮蔽与保护的说法。

entries.definition: a small sheltered bay
to want what another person has
a small green plant with three leaves
to keep something from being seen
to fold paper or cloth around a thing
entries.definitionCN: 把纸或布裹在东西外面

entries.definition: to protect from weather or harm

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a cloth over bread, then move to a book that holds a whole subject.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从盖住面包的一块布开始，再到一本包住整门学问的书。

normal.en: Co- plus over: something laid all over the top.
normal.cn: co- 加 over：把东西整个铺在上面。

normal.en: A lid covers a pot, and a cloth covers bread.
normal.cn: 盖子盖住锅，布盖住面包。

normal.en: A book covers a subject the way a sheet covers a bed.
normal.cn: 书涵盖一门学问，就像床单盖住一张床。

normal.en: Reporters cover a story by standing right over it.
normal.cn: 记者报道一件事，就是站到它正上方去看。

normal.en: The cover is the door of a book.
normal.cn: 封面就是一本书的门。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet shaken open above a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一块布在桌面上方被抖开。

abstract.en: Picture snow covering a whole field in one night.
abstract.cn: 想象一夜之间雪盖住整片田野。

abstract.en: Picture a hand held over a candle flame.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手挡在烛焰上方。

examples.en: Dust covered every shelf in the room.
examples.cn: 房间里每个架子上都盖着灰。

examples.en: The course covers both grammar and writing.
examples.cn: 这门课兼含语法与写作。

examples.en: Her photo is on the cover of the magazine.
examples.cn: 她的照片登在杂志封面上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cover 记成 co（共同）加 over（在上面）：一起盖在上面，就是把东西遮住了。

root: 源自拉丁语 cooperire（整个盖住），由 co-（完全）与 operire（关上、遮住）构成，经古法语 covrir 进入英语，本指盖住保护，后引申为涵盖、报道与封面。

sensesIntro.en: From a cloth laid over bread, to a book that holds a subject, to the front that faces you.
sensesIntro.cn: 从盖在面包上的布，到包住一门学问的书，最后到正对着你的那一面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cloth spread over everything on a table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块布铺开，盖住桌上的所有东西。

branches.en: The cloth hides and protects what lies under it.
branches.cn: 布把下面的东西遮住，也保护起来。

branches.en: A wide enough cloth holds a whole range of things.
branches.cn: 布够大，就能兜住一整套内容。

branches.en: The outermost layer is what a reader meets first.
branches.cn: 最外面那一层，是读者最先遇到的东西。

branches.en: Covering and including both mean taking something in.
branches.cn: 遮盖与包含，都是把东西收进来。

branches.en: A book covers a subject and shows its cover to the world.
branches.cn: 书包住一门学问，又把封面亮给世人。

intro.en: Cover grows from the Latin hiding base oper-, which also gives discover and uncover.
intro.cn: cover 从拉丁语表示遮盖的词基 oper- 长出来，discover 与 uncover 也由它构成。

latinIntro.en: The base operire still hides inside cover, covert and discover.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 operire 至今仍藏在 cover、covert 与 discover 里。

items.example: The road was covered with leaves.
A thin covering of snow lay outside.
The coverage of the match was wide.
items.exampleCN: 这场比赛的报道范围很广。
她把床罩叠得整整齐齐。

items.meaning: to take the cover off and find

items.exampleCN: 他揭开了那口老井的盖。

definition_en: a large female farm animal kept for milk, or to frighten someone
core_image: 一头黑白花的大牛站在草地上，尾巴来回甩动
scene: 清晨牧场上的黑白花大牛慢慢抬起头，嘴里还在嚼草。The cow stood still while the farmer milked it.
sceneCN: 这里 cow 指「奶牛」（第 2 个义项：养来产奶的牛）；句意是农夫挤奶时那头牛一动不动。

senses.title: The female of cattle
senses.definition: a large adult female of cattle
senses.definitionCN: 成年的大型雌性牛
senses.example: A cow and her calf stood in the shade.
senses.exampleCN: 一头母牛和小牛站在阴凉里。
senses.why: The female of the herd carries the next generation.
senses.whyCN: 牛群里的雌性承载着下一代。

senses.title: The animal that gives milk
senses.definition: a cow kept on a farm for its milk
senses.definitionCN: 养在农场里用来产奶的牛
senses.example: The farmer milks every cow at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫天亮时给每头奶牛挤奶。
senses.why: Milk turns a field into a daily gift.
senses.whyCN: 牛奶把一片草地变成每天的礼物。

senses.title: To frighten into obedience
senses.definition: to make someone afraid so that they obey
senses.definitionCN: 使人害怕从而服从
senses.example: He was cowed by the shouting.
senses.exampleCN: 他被那阵吼叫吓住了。
senses.why: Fear bends a person the way a yoke bends a neck.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧把人压弯，就像轭把脖子压弯。

intro.en: Cow goes back to Old English cu, from a very old Indo-European word for cattle.
intro.cn: cow 可追溯到古英语 cu，其更早来源是一个表示牛的古老印欧词。

items.en: An old root named cattle and could mean wealth.
items.cn: 一个古老词根指牛群，也可以表示财富。

items.en: The root became kuz in the Germanic languages.
items.cn: 这个词根在日耳曼诸语中变成 kuz。

items.en: Cu named the female of cattle.
items.cn: cu 指雌性的牛。

items.en: Cow stayed the everyday word for the milking animal.
items.cn: cow 一直是称呼产奶牛的口常词。

items.en: The verb to cow grew from the picture of a bent neck.
items.cn: 动词「恐吓」由脖子被压弯的形象引申而来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words close to cow in spelling, and the meaning group names other cattle words.
note.cn: 形近组收集拼写接近 cow 的词，近义组列出其他与牛有关的说法。

entries.definition: a person who runs from danger
to bend down low in fear
a hood that covers the head
cows and bulls kept in a herd
the male of cattle
a castrated bull used for work

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a slow animal chewing grass, then move to milk and to a bent neck.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一头慢慢嚼草的动物开始，再到牛奶，最后到被压弯的脖子。

normal.en: A cow stands in the field all day and turns grass into milk.
normal.cn: 母牛整天站在田里，把草变成奶。

normal.en: One cow, one calf: the herd begins with two.
normal.cn: 一头母牛一头小牛，牛群就从两头开始。

normal.en: The word is short and low, like the animal's low call.
normal.cn: 这个词又短又低，像牛发出的低沉叫声。

normal.en: To cow a person is to make their neck bend.
normal.cn: 恐吓一个人，就是让他的脖子弯下去。

normal.en: A cowboy is simply a boy who works with cows.
normal.cn: 牛仔不过就是和牛打交道的男孩。

abstract.en: Picture a black and white animal with a slow swinging tail.
abstract.cn: 想象一头黑白花、尾巴慢悠悠甩动的动物。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden bucket filling with warm milk.
abstract.cn: 想象一只木桶装满温热的奶。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy head lowered under a shouting voice.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗沉重的头在吼声中低下去。

examples.en: The cow chewed grass beside the fence.
examples.cn: 母牛在篱笆边嚼草。

examples.en: Every morning he milks the cows before six.
examples.cn: 每天早上六点前他给奶牛挤奶。

examples.en: She refused to be cowed by their threats.
examples.cn: 她拒绝被他们的威胁吓倒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cow 记成「靠」：牧场上靠着一头大母牛，慢慢嚼着草。

root: 源自古英语 cu（母牛），可追到原始日耳曼语与更早的印欧词根；动词「恐吓」由「把脖子压弯」的形象引申而来。

sensesIntro.en: From the female of the herd to the milk she gives, and at last to the fear that bends a neck.
sensesIntro.cn: 从牛群里的雌性，到她给出的牛奶，最后到把脖子压弯的恐惧。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy black and white animal standing in grass.
core.cn: 核心意象：一头黑白花的大牲口站在草地里。

branches.en: The adult female is the centre of the herd.
branches.cn: 成年的雌性是牛群的中心。

branches.en: Her milk feeds a farm every single morning.
branches.cn: 她的奶每个清晨养活一座农场。

branches.en: Fear works like a yoke on the neck of a person.
branches.cn: 恐惧像轭一样压在人脖子上。

branches.en: The animal and her gift share one short name.
branches.cn: 这动物和她的馈赠共用一个短词。

branches.en: Something gentle can still be forced to kneel.
branches.cn: 温顺的东西也可能被逼得跪下。

intro.en: Cow is a short base word that builds compounds with boy, hide, hand and bell.
intro.cn: cow 是个短词根，与 boy、hide、hand、bell 等组合成复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin named the same animal bos, a word kept in bovine.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 bos 称呼同一种动物，这个词保留在 bovine 里。

items.example: They felt cowed by the crowd.
His cowing of the staff failed.
items.exampleCN: 他吓唬员工的做法没成功。

items.example: The bag is made of cowhide.

items.meaning: a bell hung on a cow
items.example: The cowbell rang across the field.

definition_en: a thin line where something has broken, or to break with a sharp sound
core_image: 冰面上出现一道细长的白痕，越裂越长
scene: 脚一踩，湖面的冰立刻裂开一道细长的白线。The thin ice cracked under his boots.
sceneCN: 这里 crack 指「裂开」（第 2 个义项：因受力而出现裂缝）；句意是薄冰在他靴子下裂开了。

senses.title: A thin broken line
senses.definition: a thin line where something has broken but not fallen apart
senses.definitionCN: 物体破裂却还没散开时留下的细线
senses.example: There is a crack in the ceiling.
senses.exampleCN: 天花板上有一道裂缝。
senses.why: A hard thing gives a little, not all at once.
senses.whyCN: 硬东西会先让一点，不会一下子全碎。

senses.title: To break with a sound
senses.definition: to break with a sharp sound, or to develop a thin line
senses.definitionCN: 伴随脆响而破裂，或出现一道细纹
senses.example: The cup cracked when it hit the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 杯子砸到地上时裂了。
senses.why: Stone shouts when it finally gives way.
senses.whyCN: 石头最终让步时，会喊出一声。

senses.title: To solve something hard
senses.definition: to solve a difficult problem or a secret code
senses.definitionCN: 解决难题或破译秘密代码
senses.example: They cracked the code in one night.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一夜之间破解了密码。
senses.why: A hard shell must break before the kernel is reached.
senses.whyCN: 要吃到果仁，硬壳必须先破。

intro.en: Crack comes from Old English cracian, to make a sharp noise, a word shaped by the sound itself.
intro.cn: crack 源自古英语 cracian（发出脆响），这个词本身就是模仿声音造出来的。

items.en: Cracian meant to make a sharp noise.
items.cn: cracian 意为发出尖脆的声响。

items.en: Crack named the sound of something splitting.
items.cn: crack 指东西裂开时的响声。

items.en: It came to name the line left after the sound.
items.cn: 它接着用来指声音过后留下的那道线。

items.en: To crack a code borrowed the sense of breaking a shell.
items.cn: 「破解密码」借用了敲开外壳的意思。

items.en: It now covers cracks, jokes, codes and crackdowns.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖裂缝、笑话、密码与严厉打击。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers sharp-sounding words, and the meaning group names other kinds of break.
note.cn: 形近组收集带尖锐声响的词，近义组列出其他表示破裂的说法。

entries.definition: a loud violent collision
to make small repeated cracking sounds
to make a long high sound when moving
entries.definitionCN: 移动时发出又长又尖的响声

entries.definition: to divide along a line
a break in bone or hard material
an empty space between two things

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a sharp sound, then move to the line it leaves and to a code broken open.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一声脆响开始，再到它留下的细线，最后到被敲开的密码。

normal.en: Say the word aloud: crack already sounds like breaking.
normal.cn: 把这词念出来，crack 本身就带着裂开的响声。

normal.en: A crack is the echo of a break frozen in place.
normal.cn: 裂缝就是一次断裂被冻住的回声。

normal.en: A cup cracks before it ever falls apart.
normal.cn: 杯子在彻底碎掉之前会先裂。

normal.en: To crack a code is to break its hard shell.
normal.cn: 破解密码，就是敲开它坚硬的外壳。

normal.en: A cracker is named for the sound it makes between your teeth.
normal.cn: 饼干的名字，来自它在牙间发出的那声脆响。

abstract.en: Picture a white line running across grey ice.
abstract.cn: 想象一道白线在灰冰上延伸。

abstract.en: Picture a hairline scar on a porcelain plate.
abstract.cn: 想象瓷盘上一道发丝般的裂痕。

abstract.en: Picture a locked box opening with a small snap.
abstract.cn: 想象一只锁着的箱子啪一声开了。

examples.en: A crack ran across the frozen pond.
examples.cn: 一道裂缝横穿结冰的池塘。

examples.en: The branch cracked under his weight.
examples.cn: 树枝在他的重量下裂了。

examples.en: She cracked two eggs into the pan.
examples.cn: 她把两个鸡蛋打进锅里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crack 记成「咔嚓」：东西裂开时那一声脆响，就是 crack，声音之后留下裂缝。

root: 源自古英语 cracian（发出脆响），是模拟声音构成的词，本指物体裂开时的声响，后指裂缝本身，又引申出破解与打击等义。

sensesIntro.en: From the sharp sound of breaking, to the line it leaves, to a hard problem solved.
sensesIntro.cn: 从破裂的脆响，到它留下的细线，最后到被解决的难题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white line splitting a hard surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道白线把硬表面劈开。

branches.en: The line stays because the two sides still hold.
branches.cn: 裂缝留下，是因为两边还撑着。

branches.en: The moment of breaking always makes a noise.
branches.cn: 破裂的那一刻总会发出一声。

branches.en: A secret is a shell, and solving it is cracking it open.
branches.cn: 秘密是一只壳，解开它就是把它敲开。

branches.en: Sound and line are two records of the same event.
branches.cn: 声音和细线，是同一件事的两份记录。

branches.en: Both a cup and a code can give way suddenly.
branches.cn: 杯子和密码都可能突然让步。

intro.en: Crack is an imitative base word that grows tools, actions and compounds with down and pot.
intro.cn: crack 是模拟声音的词根，可与表示工具、动作以及 down、pot 的词素组合。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source; the word is native English, shaped by sound.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁语来源，是英语本族词，由声音模仿而成。

items.meaning: a thin break or its sound
items.meaningCN: 细裂缝或它发出的响声

items.meaning: the act of breaking or solving
items.example: The cracking of the code took hours.
items.exampleCN: 破解密码花了几个小时。

items.example: He ate a cracker with cheese.
items.exampleCN: 他就着奶酪吃了一块饼干。

items.example: They called the inventor a crackpot.
items.exampleCN: 他们管那位发明家叫怪人。

definition_zh: 手艺；工艺；手工艺品；船；飞行器
definition_en: skill in making things by hand, an object made that way, or a boat or aircraft
core_image: 一双手把一团泥慢慢收成一只薄壁的碗
scene: 老人把一团泥放在转盘上，双手一收，碗壁就薄了下来。Pottery is a craft that takes years to learn.
sceneCN: 这里 craft 指「手艺」（第 1 个义项：手工制作的技艺）；句意是制陶是一门需要多年才能学会的手艺。

pos.zh: 手艺；工艺；手工艺品；船；飞行器

senses.title: Skill in the hands
senses.definition: skill in making things with the hands
senses.definitionCN: 用双手制作物品的技艺
senses.example: Weaving baskets is a craft.
senses.exampleCN: 编篮子是一门手艺。
senses.why: Skill leaves the head and settles in the fingers.
senses.whyCN: 本事从脑子里下来，住进了手指里。

senses.title: Something made by hand
senses.definition: an object made by hand with skill
senses.definitionCN: 用技艺手工做成的物件
senses.example: The shelf is full of local crafts.
senses.exampleCN: 架子上摆满了本地的手工艺品。
senses.why: Each object keeps the shape of the hand that made it.
senses.whyCN: 每件物品都留着做它的那只手的形状。

senses.title: A boat or aircraft
senses.definition: a boat, ship or aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 小船、轮船或飞行器
senses.example: A small craft waited by the pier.
senses.exampleCN: 一只小船等在码头边。
senses.why: A vessel is also a made thing, shaped by skill.
senses.whyCN: 船同样是靠手艺造出来的东西。

intro.en: Craft goes back to Old English cræft, meaning strength, power or skill.
intro.cn: craft 可追溯到古英语 cræft，意为力量、能力或本领。

items.en: Cræft meant strength, power or skill.
items.cn: cræft 意为力量、能力或技艺。

items.en: The same root gave German Kraft, strength.
items.cn: 同一个词根在德语中变成 Kraft，意为力量。

items.en: Craft came to mean skill in making things.
items.cn: craft 转而指制作物品的技艺。

items.en: Craft also named a boat, a thing built with skill.
items.cn: craft 又开始指船，即靠技艺造出的东西。

items.en: It now covers hand skills, small vessels and clever making.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖手工技艺、小船与精心的制作。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words near craft in shape, and the meaning group names other words for skilled work.
note.cn: 形近组收集形状接近 craft 的词，近义组列出其他表示技艺与行业的说法。

entries.definition: clever in a way that hides the truth
a first rough version of a text
a piece of living tissue joined to another
the ability to do something well
a job that needs skilled hands
the making of beautiful things

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with clay on a wheel, then move to a shelf of made things and to a small boat.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从转盘上的泥开始，再到一架子手作，最后到一只小船。

normal.en: Craft first meant strength, and strength moved into the fingers.
normal.cn: craft 最初指力量，后来这股力量走进了手指。

normal.en: A crooked bowl still shows the hand that made it.
normal.cn: 一只歪碗也还看得出做它的那只手。

normal.en: Practise a craft daily and the hands remember.
normal.cn: 每天练一门手艺，手就会记住。

normal.en: A small craft on the water is a boat built by skill.
normal.cn: 水面上的小船，就是靠技艺造出来的船。

normal.en: To craft a plan is to shape it like clay.
normal.cn: 精心制定计划，就是像捏泥一样把它塑出来。

abstract.en: Picture ten fingers closing around wet clay.
abstract.cn: 想象十根手指合拢在一块湿泥上。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden shelf of bowls, each slightly different.
abstract.cn: 想象一木架碗，每只都略有不同。

abstract.en: Picture a thin hull sliding into grey water.
abstract.cn: 想象一只薄壳船滑进灰色的水里。

examples.en: She learned the craft of glass blowing.
examples.cn: 她学会了吹玻璃的手艺。

examples.en: The crafts on sale were all made by hand.
examples.cn: 出售的手工艺品全是手工做的。

examples.en: The harbour held a hundred small craft.
examples.cn: 港口停着一百只小船。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 craft 记成 c（手）加 raft（筏子）：用手扎出一只筏子，靠的就是手艺。

root: 源自古英语 cræft（力量、技能），与德语 Kraft（力量）同源，本指力气与本领，后专指手工技艺，又用来指靠技艺造出的船与飞行器。

sensesIntro.en: From skill in the fingers, to the object made, to the vessel shaped by that skill.
sensesIntro.cn: 从手指里的技艺，到做成的物件，最后到靠这门技艺造出的船。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands drawing a shape out of soft clay.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手从软泥里拉出一个形状。

branches.en: Skill lives in repeated motion until it becomes sure.
branches.cn: 技艺活在反复的动作里，直到变得稳妥。

branches.en: The finished object carries the marks of its maker.
branches.cn: 做成的东西带着制作者的印记。

branches.en: Even a boat is a hand-shaped thing on water.
branches.cn: 连船也只是水上一件用手塑成的东西。

branches.en: Skill and object are the cause and the proof.
branches.cn: 技艺是因，物件是证。

branches.en: From a bowl to a boat, all are made by the same care.
branches.cn: 从碗到船，都出自同一种用心。

intro.en: Craft is a native base word that joins man, work and ship to name people and products.
intro.cn: craft 是本族词根，可与 man、work、ship 等组合，指人与制品。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source is needed: craft is Germanic, like German Kraft.
latinIntro.cn: 它无需拉丁来源：craft 属日耳曼语，与德语 Kraft 同源。

items.exampleCN: 集市上展出本地手工艺品。

items.meaning: the act of making by hand
items.exampleCN: 手工制作需要安静的几个小时。

items.meaning: a person skilled in a craft

items.exampleCN: 这张桌子显出精湛的做工。

items.example: A crafty answer avoided the question.
items.exampleCN: 一个狡猾的回答绕开了问题。
